newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking pushes Delhi stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pushes Delhi stocks to lower close.

text.p: Delhi stocks closed lower on Wednesday on selling by profit-takers coupled with the absence of any factor to encourage buyers, brokers said.
They said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were somewhat active and bought stocks of Indian Rayon, Hero Honda and a few other companies while domestic investors were keen sellers.
The benchmark index dropped 9.61 points to close at 769.11 points.

"Hectic activity in Indian Rayon following the company's proposal to issue one bonus share for every two shares held was the only feature of today's session," said S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit.
Indian Rayon, which announced its bonus issue on Tuesday, rose 20 rupees to 380 while Hero Honda firmed up 26.50 rupees to 377.50 rupees, brokers said.
Reliance fell 2.65 rupees to 300.60 while State Bank of India closed 2.25 rupees lower at 304.25.
ACC lost 49 rupees to 1,310 on selling by speculators anticipating discouraging annual results, brokers said.
